prior_block:
PRICE PRIORS for recurring line types (statistical model fitted on the thresholds t revealed
in earlier games; gross amounts). How to use them:
- The amounts are final thresholds as they were revealed: they already contain whatever
  deductible, VAT and customary-price judgement applied in those cases, and they were computed
  from the full invoiced quantity (the whole quantity was indemnified there). For an
  indemnified line of this type take the stated amount for the line as t as it stands and give
  a price_log_sd that matches the stated range. Do not deduct a deductible from it and do not
  cut the invoiced quantity.
- Deviate only for something this case has and those cases did not: an aggregate cap or
  sub-limit that the lines of this invoice must share, a percentage reduction for a breached
  duty, or a purchase price or sum insured stated in the claim that limits the line.
- Whether a line is indemnified in THIS case is decided by the policy and the claim, not by
  the history. The history only says how often this line type was paid at all. A line type
  that was never indemnified before is usually an ancillary charge the policies do not carry;
  treat it as indemnified only if this policy clearly says so.
- line 1 "Bicycle frame replacement": indemnified in 1 of 2 earlier cases, t = 0 in 1; when indemnified t per pc about 229 (80% range 142 to 392); revealed per pc: 142-349 (case 24)
- line 2 "Bicycle brake replacement": indemnified in 1 of 2 earlier cases, t = 0 in 1; when indemnified t per pc about 140 (80% range 104 to 211); revealed per pc: 130-148 (case 24)
- line 6 "Shipping": indemnified in 1 of 8 earlier cases, t = 0 in 7; when indemnified t per pc about 26 (80% range 19.2 to 39); revealed per pc: 24-27 (case 24)
- line 7 "Vehicle costs": indemnified in 14 of 29 earlier cases, t = 0 in 15; when indemnified t per pc about 77 (80% range 57 to 95); revealed per pc: >=74 (case 27*), 37-41 (case 32*), >=83 (case 34*), >=76 (case 34*), >=65 (case 39*), >=71 (case 40*) (* = other policy wording)
- line 8 "Assembly costs": indemnified in 3 of 5 earlier cases, t = 0 in 2; when indemnified t per pc about 113 (80% range 92 to 151); revealed per pc: >=100 (case 23*), 106-209 (case 24), >=97 (case 24) (* = other policy wording)
- line 9 "Miscellaneous items": NOT indemnified (t = 0) in all 4 earlier cases; no price evidence
- line 10 "Apprentice hours": indemnified in 1 of 5 earlier cases, t = 0 in 4; when indemnified t per hr about 55 (80% range 29 to 139); revealed per hr: 35-36 (case 23*) (* = other policy wording)
- line 11 "Skilled worker hours": indemnified in 3 of 7 earlier cases, t = 0 in 4; when indemnified t per hr about 39 (80% range 32 to 50); revealed per hr: 50-58 (case 36*), 35-42 (case 24), 35-40 (case 26) (* = other policy wording)
- line 13 "Cut and remove seized lock to release bicycle": indemnified in the one earlier case; when indemnified t per pc about 54 (80% range 40 to 82); revealed per pc: >=50 (case 26), so this line (2 pc) about 108 (80 to 165)
- line 14 "Vehicle costs – return visit": NOT indemnified (t = 0) in all 4 earlier cases; no price evidence
- line 16 "Administrative and claim-processing fee": NOT indemnified (t = 0) in all 7 earlier cases; no price evidence
- line 17 "Apprentice hours": indemnified in 1 of 5 earlier cases, t = 0 in 4; when indemnified t per hr about 55 (80% range 29 to 139); revealed per hr: 35-36 (case 23*) (* = other policy wording)

items.rationale: Theft peril is covered; the frame was physically damaged in the theft (2.3.1(b)), so repair/replacement is indemnified as a necessary repair cost (7.1.1(b)), but subject to the EUR 500 mobility equipment sub-limit (4.2.2) shared with other indemnifiable lines.

Brakes were physically damaged in the theft (2.3.1(b)), so repair/replacement is indemnified as a necessary repair cost (7.1.1(b)), but subject to the EUR 500 mobility equipment sub-limit (4.2.2) shared with other indemnifiable lines.
Tracker was not itself an affected item (not taken or damaged in the theft); replacement is an addition/supplement (3.1.7, 7.1.8(b)), so not indemnified.
Second bike was not affected by the theft; service is maintenance/upkeep (3.1.6, 7.1.8(a)), so not indemnified.
Helmet and lights are accessories/supplementary equipment not themselves affected by the theft (3.1.7, 4.2.3, 7.1.8(b)), so not indemnified.

Shipping of the recovered/damaged bike is a necessary element of restoring the affected item (7.1.7(f)), but subject to the EUR 500 mobility equipment sub-limit (4.2.2) shared with other indemnifiable lines.

Vehicle costs for the recovery/repair of the affected bike are ancillary to the covered work (7.1.7(g)), but subject to the EUR 500 mobility equipment sub-limit (4.2.2) shared with other indemnifiable lines.
Assembly is part of the necessary repair of the affected bike (7.1.7(c)), but subject to the EUR 500 mobility equipment sub-limit (4.2.2) shared with other indemnifiable lines.
Miscellaneous items are not specified as relating to the affected item or necessary repair/recovery; historically never indemnified (see priors), so not indemnified.
Labour for repair/recovery of the affected bike is indemnified (7.1.7(d)), but subject to the EUR 500 mobility equipment sub-limit (4.2.2) shared with other indemnifiable lines.

items.description: Cut and remove seized lock to release bicycle
items.rationale: Cutting the lock to recover the bike is a recovery cost under 5.2.2(b), but subject to the EUR 500 mobility equipment sub-limit (4.2.2) shared with other indemnifiable lines.
Vehicle costs for a return visit are not indemnified (see priors and 7.1.8(f)), as only the necessary attendance for the covered work is indemnified.

Administrative and claim-processing fees are explicitly excluded (3.1.5, 7.1.8(d)), so not indemnified.
